## AuditEntry

AuditEntry is one recorded operation, as it was recorded: the log is append-only and nothing here is derived at read time except the actor's email, which is joined so a reader is not handed a UUID to look up by hand.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |
| `actorId` | string | actor_id is empty for an operation nobody was signed in for - a failed login, a runner registering itself - and for one whose user has since been deleted. |
| `actorEmail` | string | actor_email is empty for the same reasons, and is what the user's row says now rather than what it said then. |
| `action` | string |  |
| `resourceType` | string |  |
| `resourceId` | string | resource_id is empty for an operation with no row to point at - a failed login, a change to the installation's settings. resource_type still says what kind of thing it was about. |
| `details` | string | details is the JSON the operation recorded, verbatim. It has no schema: what a login records and what a team membership change records have nothing in common, and a reader that insists on a shape would have to be changed by every new action. |
| `ipAddress` | string |  |
| `createdAt` | `Timestamp` |  |

## BrokeredRequest

BrokeredRequest is one request the egress proxy read from the workspace's machine to a brokered name. No header and no body: what the proxy set is the team's secret, and what the machine sent is its own.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |
| `method` | string |  |
| `path` | string | As the machine sent it, without the query. |
| `status` | integer (int32) | What the real host answered; what the proxy answered for a refusal. |
| `bytesSent` | string (int64) |  |
| `bytesReceived` | string (int64) |  |
| `at` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `refused` | string | Empty for a request passed on. Otherwise why the proxy refused it: credentials (a secret or token the team does not hold), host (a request for another name), upgrade, method (TRACE or TRACK), scope (a method or path the injecting rule does not allow), authority (the cloud principal refused to sign it). |
| `principal` | string | Who asked: "user" or "agent", by the listener the proxy read it on. |

## BurstMode

BurstMode is how a workspace of a preset may grow past what it starts with. - `BURST_MODE_FIXED`: FIXED starts at the preset's size and stays there. - `BURST_MODE_TO_PRESET`: TO_PRESET starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to its size. - `BURST_MODE_TO_HOST`: TO_HOST starts at the preset's burst floor and may grow to everything its host has.

One of: `BURST_MODE_UNSPECIFIED`, `BURST_MODE_FIXED`, `BURST_MODE_TO_PRESET`, `BURST_MODE_TO_HOST`.

## CostMonth

One month of the trend on Admin → Costs, in millionths of the bill's currency. An estimate of what nobody caused, from the reading it names: a month's last days are revised by the cloud into the next, and read again until they settle.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `month` | `Timestamp` | Its first instant, UTC. |
| `readAt` | `Timestamp` | The reading its costs are from. |
| `currency` | string | ISO 4217. |
| `totalMicros` | string (int64) | Every cost of its days; idle and unstored are parts of it. |
| `idleMicros` | string (int64) | What the runners cost that no workspace held. |
| `unstoredMicros` | string (int64) | What the volumes' bucket cost for bytes no workspace keeps. |
| `budgetLimitMicros` | string or null (int64) | The installation's budget as the month's last reading in it said; unset where it had none. |

## CostShare

What was caused in a month of the cloud's bill, as the installation shares it out (AdminService.GetCosts): by one workspace, or by several summed. In millionths of the bill's currency. A share is of days already billed, never of this hour: the bill is read from the cloud a few times a day.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `computeMicros` | string (int64) | Of the runners: what was held of them. |
| `storageMicros` | string (int64) | Of the volumes' bucket: what the volumes kept. |
| `sentBytes` | string (int64) | What the traffic came to in the month: the machine's network out and back, and its sessions through the relay, both ways. Counted, not costed. |
| `receivedBytes` | string (int64) |  |
| `forwardedBytes` | string (int64) |  |

## DeletionFate

DeletionFate is what a delete does to one thing a workspace has. - `DELETION_FATE_ERASED`: Gone when the delete is done, and not undeleted. - `DELETION_FATE_TRASHED`: In the trash for GetWorkspaceDeletionResponse.trash_days, restored by an undelete, erased when they are up. - `DELETION_FATE_KEPT`: Outlives the workspace, the trash's days included.

One of: `DELETION_FATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `DELETION_FATE_ERASED`, `DELETION_FATE_TRASHED`, `DELETION_FATE_KEPT`.

## DepartureFate

DepartureFate is what taking a host out does to one workspace on it. - `DEPARTURE_FATE_MOVES`: Suspended with its memory and resumed on another runner with room. - `DEPARTURE_FATE_STAYS`: Keeps its place on this runner: a drain moves only what runs. - `DEPARTURE_FATE_LOSES_PLACE`: Suspended at a published snapshot: its disk is let go of here, and its next start is on another runner, from what it published. - `DEPARTURE_FATE_HOLDS`: It keeps the host: the removal is refused while it is here. A group's machine is held by a disk only here, until it is stopped, which publishes it, or moved; a revoked host by any workspace that names it. - `DEPARTURE_FATE_STOPS`: Its disk is only here and is left here: it runs again only once recovered onto another runner, giving up what this one had not published.

One of: `DEPARTURE_FATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `DEPARTURE_FATE_MOVES`, `DEPARTURE_FATE_STAYS`, `DEPARTURE_FATE_LOSES_PLACE`, `DEPARTURE_FATE_HOLDS`, `DEPARTURE_FATE_STOPS`.

One of: `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`, `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_PENDING`, `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_COMPLETE`, `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_EXPIRED`, `DEVICE_LOGIN_STATUS_DENIED`.

## HeaderInjection

HeaderInjection is a header the egress proxy sets: header, to prefix and then a value the workspace never holds - a team secret's, or a token of the workspace's identity. One of the two.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `header` | string |  |
| `secret` | string | The team secret's name. |
| `prefix` | string | What goes before the value, as "Bearer ". |
| `identity` | string | The audience of a token of the workspace's identity, issued for the proxy to present: bound to no key, and saying so (spin.via = egress-proxy). |
| `forge` | string | The forge whose credential goes in the header, whole: "github" is the workspace owner's own token, connected through the installation's OAuth App (ForgeService), which the control plane keeps and refreshes. |
| `methods` | list of string | The requests the header is set on: these methods, and paths under path_prefix by whole segments. Another request to the rule's names is answered 403. None of either is every request. |
| `pathPrefix` | string |  |

## HealthPart

HealthPart is which part of the installation a check is of. - `HEALTH_PART_DATABASE`: The control plane's database answers a query. - `HEALTH_PART_DATABASE_ARCHIVE`: The database's continuous archive keeps up: its last WAL file sent and how many wait. Its base backups are taken by a timer outside the control plane, which records nothing it can read. - `HEALTH_PART_LOG_STORE`: The log store (Quickwit) beside the control plane answers that it is ready. - `HEALTH_PART_COLLECTOR`: The collector sends what it is given: spans to the trace store, samples to the metric store (GetTelemetryStatus). It is what says whether the metric store takes writes - the control plane is not one of the metric store's readers. - `HEALTH_PART_JOBS`: The control plane's periodic work: a job whose last run failed (ListJobs). - `HEALTH_PART_HOSTS`: The hosts registered and not taken out of the fleet: those whose command stream is not up, and those that answer and fail a check of their own (HostCheck). - `HEALTH_PART_WAITING_WORKSPACES`: Workspaces waiting for a runner, across the whole fleet.

One of: `HEALTH_PART_UNSPECIFIED`, `HEALTH_PART_DATABASE`, `HEALTH_PART_DATABASE_ARCHIVE`, `HEALTH_PART_LOG_STORE`, `HEALTH_PART_COLLECTOR`, `HEALTH_PART_JOBS`, `HEALTH_PART_HOSTS`, `HEALTH_PART_WAITING_WORKSPACES`.

## HealthReport

HealthReport is what the supervisor inside a workspace observes about it. Here rather than beside the stream that carries it, for the reason SupervisorState is here: it is read from both sides - reported by the supervisor on its own connection (spin.agent.v1), and returned to an operator by WorkspaceService.GetWorkspaceStatus. It is also what keeps the dependency between the two packages pointing one way. spin.v1 is the vocabulary and spin.agent.v1 is the machine surface built on it; a type the operator's side needs from the agent's side would make each package need the other.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `healthy` | boolean |  |
| `checks` | list of [HealthCheckResult](/reference/api/types/#healthcheckresult) |  |

## HealthStatus

- `HEALTH_STATUS_DEGRADED`: Working, and something in it wants a look: some hosts not connected, a job's last run failed, a workspace waiting longer than a machine takes to boot. - `HEALTH_STATUS_FAILED`: Not doing what it is for: the database does not answer, the archive's last send failed, no host is connected.

One of: `HEALTH_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`, `HEALTH_STATUS_OK`, `HEALTH_STATUS_DEGRADED`, `HEALTH_STATUS_FAILED`.

## Host

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |
| `address` | string |  |
| `state` | [HostState](/reference/api/types/#hoststate) |  |
| `capacity` | [Resources](/reference/api/types/#resources) |  |
| `allocated` | [Resources](/reference/api/types/#resources) |  |
| `workspaceCount` | integer (int32) |  |
| `agentVersion` | string |  |
| `labels` | map of string to string |  |
| `lastHeartbeat` | `Timestamp` | last_heartbeat is whichever of this host's two channels was heard from last, and they are not the same thing: the command stream carries what the host can be \*told\* (start this, stop that), and the volume agent's own heartbeat renews the lease its disks are served under. Either refreshes this, so a fresh stamp says one of them is alive and not which: stream_heard_at and lease_renewed_at are each on its own. It is what the sweep that forgets a host gone for good reads. |
| `registeredAt` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `connected` | boolean | connected is the command stream, now: the half that decides whether this host can be given a workspace or asked to stop one. A host whose stream is gone while its volume agent keeps renewing reads as freshly heartbeated above and can be told nothing at all - which is the state an operator is looking at when they ask why a host takes no work. |
| `goingAway` | boolean | going_away is this host on its way out: a runner told the control plane it is stopping - an operator's restart, or the cloud taking the machine away - and it takes no new workspace from that moment. Nothing is written to the database for it (a state there would outlive the restart it described), so this is the only place an operator can see that the host they are looking at is leaving rather than idle. |
| `checks` | list of [HostCheck](/reference/api/types/#hostcheck) | checks are what the host last found when it asked itself whether a workspace can run on it as it should, as its heartbeat said: held for as long as the host is connected, like going_away, and empty for a host that has said nothing yet. |
| `hostClass` | string | host_class is the class (HostClass.name) of the group that launched the machine, which ties the host to its FleetClass: "default" for a machine no group launched. |
| `machineVersion` | string | machine_version is the spin-machine release the host registered (its QEMU, kernel and firmware); empty for a host with no machine. |
| `detected` | [Resources](/reference/api/types/#resources) | detected is what the host found it has when it last registered (cores, memory, disk GB), beside capacity, which is what it advertises: a HostPolicy capacity holds a machine back by saying it has less. Zero for a host that has not registered since it was made. |
| `streamHeardAt` | `Timestamp` | Each channel on its own. stream_heard_at is the command stream's last heartbeat the control plane recorded - unset for a host that never held one - and lease_renewed_at the volume agent's last renewal of the lease its disks are served under, unset for one that never held a lease. A host whose stream is gone while its lease renews serves its disks and can be told nothing. |
| `leaseRenewedAt` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `connectedChangedAt` | `Timestamp` | connected_changed_at is when connected last changed, as this control plane saw it: the stream registering while connected, its end while not. Unset where this control plane has seen neither since it started - stream_heard_at then says when the host was last heard. Held in memory, as connected is: a control plane that restarts starts again. |
| `streamEnd` | [HostStreamEnd](/reference/api/types/#hoststreamend) | Why the host's last command stream ended, while it is not connected; UNSPECIFIED while it is connected, and where this control plane has not seen one end. stream_end_detail is the error the stream ended with, in its own words. |
| `streamEndDetail` | string |  |
| `hostname` | string | hostname is the name the host's machine goes by, as it last registered it: how a person tells one host from another where its id says nothing. Empty for a host that has not registered since it was made. |
| `removal` | [HostRemoval](/reference/api/types/#hostremoval) | removal is how this host leaves the fleet, decided by where it came from: the only removal the API takes for it, so the dashboard offers that one and no other. |
| `removalRefused` | string | removal_refused is why that removal cannot run now - a workspace whose disk is there - in words an administrator acts on; empty while it can. |
| `keysGiven` | integer (int32) | keys_given is how many teams' disks this host was given the key of: what revoking it, or removing it as taken, marks for re-keying. |
| `machineId` | string | Where the host's machine is, as its cloud said when the host joined - never as the host said of itself: the machine's id and type as that cloud names them, its zone and its region. Each empty for a host that joined with no cloud (a registration token: a development stack, a machine of one's own), and for what its cloud did not say. |
| `machineType` | string |  |
| `zone` | string |  |
| `region` | string |  |
| `reclaimable` | boolean or null | reclaimable is whether the cloud may take the machine back, as its cloud said of the instance when it joined - a spot machine is, whatever its class says: a group that fell back to on-demand, or one whose class was changed, starts machines its class does not describe. Unset where nothing says: a host that joined with no cloud, or one its cloud named nothing of. |
| `holders` | list of [HostHolder](/reference/api/types/#hostholder) | holders is what keeps this host in the fleet, from the database: the workspaces whose disk is only here - whichever list of theirs leaves them out, a prebuild's build, a team's, another person's, a failed one - and the volumes still here that are no such workspace's disk, a trashed workspace's or an agent's home, each of which forgetting the host must detach first. At most 10; holder_count is how many there are. |
| `holderCount` | integer (int32) |  |

## HostCheck

HostCheck is one thing a host asks itself about, at start and every few minutes: a clock that is not synchronised, a KVM it cannot open, a resolver that answers its workspaces nothing - each a host that looks healthy to every other signal and fails its workspaces.

|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | name is what was checked: clock, kvm, resolver. |
| `ok` | boolean |  |
| `detail` | string | detail is what it found when it is not ok, in the host's words. |
| `checkedAt` | `Timestamp` |  |

## HostClass

A kind of runner: the shape of the machines a group of the installation's cloud starts for it, which the control plane makes and sizes. What a machine boots is the installation's launch template, never this. "default" is the class a preset that names none runs on.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Lower-case letters, digits and -, a letter first, up to 31: it is part of the group's name. |
| `description` | string |  |
| `instanceTypes` | list of string | The instance types it may be, as the cloud names them, patterns allowed ("c8id.\*"); none is any type the rest admits. |
| `vcpusMin` | integer (int32) |  |
| `vcpusMax` | integer (int32) |  |
| `memoryMibPerVcpu` | integer (int32) | The least memory a vCPU of it has, in MiB; 0 is 2048. |
| `spot` | boolean | A machine the cloud may take back (each host drains first), or an on-demand one. |
| `maxHosts` | integer (int32) | The most hosts of it; 0 is no limit of its own (the setting autoscaling_max_hosts bounds them all). |
| `fallbackOnDemand` | boolean | A spot class whose group the cloud refuses spot machines for capacity starts on-demand ones for a while, and then spot again (FleetClass.on_demand_until); spot itself is not changed. Off, the class's workspaces wait until somebody changes spot. Only a spot class has it. |

HostDeparture is what draining the host, and removing it as Host.removal says, would do to each workspace that names it - the ones a drain moves, the ones that stay, the ones that lose their place on it and the ones that hold it - so the confirmation says it before it is done.

## HostHolderKind

HostHolderKind is what a holder is, which says which list of whose shows it. - `HOST_HOLDER_KIND_WORKSPACE`: A person's own workspace, in their workspaces list. - `HOST_HOLDER_KIND_TEAM_WORKSPACE`: A workspace of a team, in its members' lists. - `HOST_HOLDER_KIND_PREBUILD_BUILD`: A prebuild's build: kept stopped as its prebuild's anchor, and in nobody's list. - `HOST_HOLDER_KIND_TRASHED_WORKSPACE`: The disk of a workspace in its owner's trash. - `HOST_HOLDER_KIND_AGENT_HOME`: A person's agent's home (AgentVolume).

HostPolicy is what an installation decides about one host. An unset field is the installation saying nothing about that setting, which leaves the host on its own default - not the same as setting it to nothing.

| `capacityDiskGb` | integer or null (int32) |  |
| `maxWorkspaceCpuCores` | integer or null (int32) | The ceiling one workspace may grow to here, for the machines it starts afterwards. |
| `maxWorkspaceMemoryMb` | integer or null (int32) |  |
| `revision` | string | revision names the content, and is what a host reports it is running under. |
| `writebackLimitBytes` | string or null (int64) | The host's writeback thresholds (spin.agent.v1.HostPolicy says why): both or neither, the background below the limit. Unset is what the host booted with. |

| `runningRevision` | string | running_revision is what the host last said, empty where it has not said or is not connected. Different from revision is a policy still on its way, which is normal for the seconds after a write and a fault after that. |
| `maxWorkspaceIoMbPerSecond` | integer or null (int32) | What one machine may read and write per second here, in MiB and in operations, for the machines it starts afterwards. Unset is no bound. |
| `maxWorkspaceIoOpsPerSecond` | integer or null (int32) |  |

## HostRemoval

HostRemoval is how a host leaves the fleet. - `HOST_REMOVAL_REVOKE`: A host registered with a token, or a machine of a cloud no group of this installation sizes: RevokeRunner. Nothing else can take its machine away. - `HOST_REMOVAL_GIVE_BACK`: A machine of an autoscaling group, connected: RemoveHost gives it back to its group, which terminates it and is asked for one less. Revoking it would leave the machine running and paid for, in a group that counts it. - `HOST_REMOVAL_FORGET`: A machine of an autoscaling group, not connected: RemoveHost gives back a machine the group still has, and forgets the host now rather than once it has been silent for host_forget_after_hours.

One of: `HOST_REMOVAL_UNSPECIFIED`, `HOST_REMOVAL_REVOKE`, `HOST_REMOVAL_GIVE_BACK`, `HOST_REMOVAL_FORGET`.

## HostShellState

- `HOST_SHELL_STATE_REQUESTED`: Asked for, waiting for a second administrator. - `HOST_SHELL_STATE_EMPTYING`: Approved: the host is cordoned and its workspaces are being suspended to run elsewhere. - `HOST_SHELL_STATE_OPEN`: Open: a terminal may attach until closes_at. - `HOST_SHELL_STATE_ENDED`: Over: closed, or past its time. Its host is retired. - `HOST_SHELL_STATE_REFUSED`: Refused, or withdrawn before it was approved. Its host was never touched.

One of: `HOST_SHELL_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `HOST_SHELL_STATE_REQUESTED`, `HOST_SHELL_STATE_EMPTYING`, `HOST_SHELL_STATE_OPEN`, `HOST_SHELL_STATE_ENDED`, `HOST_SHELL_STATE_REFUSED`.

## HostState

HostState mirrors internal/lifecycle.HostState (§28.1) and the CHECK on hosts.state: one vocabulary for the fleet, whichever component is asking. Only ACTIVE takes new work; a CORDONED or DRAINING host keeps serving (and keeps its lease) while it is evacuated, and the Agent needs to be told which of the two it is. It replaces a second set of names this schema carried for the same states - HEALTHY, DEGRADED, OFFLINE - where DEGRADED was a word nothing branched on and no name said "an operator stopped this host".

One of: `HOST_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `HOST_STATE_ACTIVE`, `HOST_STATE_CORDONED`, `HOST_STATE_DRAINING`, `HOST_STATE_DEAD`.

## HostStreamEnd

HostStreamEnd is why a host's command stream ended. - `HOST_STREAM_END_HOST_CLOSED`: The host closed it: a runner stopping or restarting. - `HOST_STREAM_END_LOST`: The connection went without the host closing it: a network fault, a runner killed, a machine that went away, a transport that timed out. - `HOST_STREAM_END_CONTROL_PLANE_CLOSED`: The control plane closed it: the host was revoked, or a newer stream of it replaced this one. - `HOST_STREAM_END_TOO_FAST`: The host sent far faster than any runner does, and was cut off. - `HOST_STREAM_END_REFUSED_RELEASE`: Its registration was refused: the host runs another release than the control plane's. - `HOST_STREAM_END_ERROR`: Its registration could not be recorded, or the stream failed in a way none of the above says.

One of: `HOST_STREAM_END_UNSPECIFIED`, `HOST_STREAM_END_HOST_CLOSED`, `HOST_STREAM_END_LOST`, `HOST_STREAM_END_CONTROL_PLANE_CLOSED`, `HOST_STREAM_END_TOO_FAST`, `HOST_STREAM_END_REFUSED_RELEASE`, `HOST_STREAM_END_ERROR`.

| `name` | string | What a person choosing a disk is shown: its name ("base image") and what it is ready for. An empty name is a publication made before one was asked for; show the ref. |

| `name` | string |  |
| `hosts` | list of [HostNetworkPolicy](/reference/api/types/#hostnetworkpolicy) | What each host reporting this tag says it enforces. |
| `declared` | boolean | declared says the installation has this policy, and rules are what it allows. A policy with no hosts is declared and not yet enforced anywhere. |
| `rules` | list of [NetworkRule](/reference/api/types/#networkrule) |  |
| `teamId` | string | The team whose admins declared it, which only its workspaces and those of the teams below it may run under; empty is the installation's. |

## NetworkPolicyRule

NetworkPolicyRule is a policy as an administrator writes it, in the words the config file takes: a name, which is a tag - letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 - and the rules it allows, each these destinations on these ports. A policy with no rules allows nothing.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |
| `rules` | list of [NetworkRule](/reference/api/types/#networkrule) |  |

## NetworkRule

NetworkRule is one thing a network policy allows: these destinations on these ports. Within a rule the two intersect - every destination on every port - and a policy is the union of its rules, so "53/udp to one resolver and 443 to github.com" is two rules and not a product of both. Here and not beside a policy for the reason HealthReport is: the control plane's policy, the one a host reports it enforces and the one a host is given are one vocabulary.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `allow` | list of string | IPv4 prefixes in CIDR. |
| `allowNames` | list of string | Names, exact or with a leading "\*.": the host opens the address its own resolver answers a machine with, for as long as the answer lives. |
| `ports` | list of string | Destination ports as "443" (TCP, which is what a bare number means), "443/udp", a range as "8000-8100" or "8000-8100/udp", or "icmp" for a ping. None is every port, at the destinations above; none of those is every destination, on these ports. |
| `broker` | boolean | The host's egress proxy stands in for these names, on HTTPS only: a machine reaches them through it and never directly, and it adds what the machine never holds. Names only. |
| `inject` | list of [HeaderInjection](/reference/api/types/#headerinjection) | Headers the proxy sets on a brokered rule's requests, each from a secret of the workspace's team (or the nearest team above it with one by that name). Brokered rules only. |
| `cloud` | [CloudAccess](/reference/api/types/#cloudaccess) | The principal the proxy authorizes a brokered rule's requests as, on its cloud: the host takes its credentials as the workspace, with a token of its identity. Brokered rules naming that cloud's endpoints only, and not with inject. |
| `verifySni` | boolean | The host's egress proxy reads the TLS server name of each connection to these names and passes on, untouched, only one this rule names: an address shared with other names opens only these to a client that says which it wants. A connection with no name, or one hiding it (ECH), goes nowhere. Names only, on TCP, never with broker; it does not stop a client that lies. |
| `principal` | string | Whose connections a brokered rule stands in for: "agent" (the workspace's agent, whose packets its guest marks), "user" (everything else the workspace sends), or "any" (empty: both). Two rules for one name, one per principal, each with its own injections and methods, say what the person may do and what the agent may. Brokered rules only: an agent reaches nothing outside the proxy, so a rule that is not brokered is the person's already. |

## PasskeyPurpose

PasskeyPurpose is what a ceremony's challenge is for. - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_REGISTER`: A passkey registered: the registration answers it. Subject: none. - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_PASSKEY`: Another passkey registered while the account has one: an assertion of one it has answers it. Subject: the new credential's id, base64url. - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_SSH_KEY`: An SSH key added (SSHKeyService.AddSSHKey). Subject: the key, in authorized_keys form. - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_DELETE_PASSKEY`: A passkey deleted. Subject: its id. - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_GUEST`: A guest let into a workspace (WorkspaceService.AddWorkspaceGuest). Subject: "&lt;workspace id> &lt;email>". - `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_CREATE_EXEC_KEY`: An API key made with workspace:exec (AuthService.CreateAPIKey), which is a shell in every workspace of its person's. Subject: the key's name.

One of: `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_UNSPECIFIED`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_REGISTER`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_PASSKEY`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_SSH_KEY`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_DELETE_PASSKEY`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_ADD_GUEST`, `PASSKEY_PURPOSE_CREATE_EXEC_KEY`.

## PortAccess

Who may reach a published port. Per port rather than per workspace: one workspace serves a demo anyone may see and an admin panel only its owner may, and a single setting for both makes the safe answer for one the wrong answer for the other. UNSPECIFIED is not a level and is never stored - the column's CHECK excludes it. A request that leaves it at proto3's zero is treated as PRIVATE, which is the direction to be wrong in: the cost of failing closed is a confusing error, and the cost of failing open is a port somebody published without meaning to. - `PORT_ACCESS_PRIVATE`: Only the workspace's owner, who must be signed in. - `PORT_ACCESS_WHITELIST`: The owner, and the users the owner granted. See GrantPortAccess. - `PORT_ACCESS_PUBLIC`: Anyone, with no session at all. Nothing is asked and nobody is redirected to a login. Until the workspace stops or fails: then the port is PRIVATE again, and made public again when it is meant to be.

One of: `PORT_ACCESS_UNSPECIFIED`, `PORT_ACCESS_PRIVATE`, `PORT_ACCESS_WHITELIST`, `PORT_ACCESS_PUBLIC`.

## ProblemAction

ProblemAction is something the console can do about a problem, each an RPC it has. - `PROBLEM_ACTION_CORDON_HOST`: DrainHost without suspend: the host takes no new workspace and keeps what it runs. - `PROBLEM_ACTION_DRAIN_HOST`: DrainHost with suspend: its workspaces are moved to other hosts. - `PROBLEM_ACTION_RUN_JOB`: RunJobNow: the job is run again, now. - `PROBLEM_ACTION_RECOVER_WORKSPACE`: RecoverUserWorkspace, of each workspace the problem names: its disk is on a host that is gone, and it runs again only once moved off it.

One of: `PROBLEM_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED`, `PROBLEM_ACTION_CORDON_HOST`, `PROBLEM_ACTION_DRAIN_HOST`, `PROBLEM_ACTION_RUN_JOB`, `PROBLEM_ACTION_RECOVER_WORKSPACE`.

One that never did - it failed, or was deleted first - is not counted, and neither is one opened from a prebuild: this is what opening without one costs. A workspace whose first boots failed its project counts from its create to the boot that went.

## Resources

Resource allocation for workspaces. Initial values (cpu_cores, memory_mb) are used at boot time. Max values control scaling limits: - 0 = unlimited (burstable to host capacity) - >0 = hard limit (cannot exceed)

| `memoryMb` | integer (int32) | Initial memory in MB at boot (default: 512) |
| `diskGb` | integer (int32) | Disk size in GB (default: 10) |
| `maxCpuCores` | integer (int32) | Max CPU cores (0 = unlimited) |
| `maxMemoryMb` | integer (int32) | Max memory in MB (0 = unlimited) |
| `bandwidthMbps` | integer (int32) | What a workspace's network carries each way, in megabits a second (0 = unshaped): its preset's, held on its host by a token bucket on each way out of its machine's namespace. Its vsock - ssh, the editor, forwarded ports - is not shaped. |

## SettingReach

SettingReach is what a saved installation setting touches, and when: each setting's definition declares one (internal/controlplane/settings), so the screen that edits it can say so before the save. - `SETTING_REACH_RUNNING_WORKSPACES`: The workspaces running now, at the control plane's next look at them. - `SETTING_REACH_NEW_WORKSPACES`: Workspaces created from now on; those that exist keep what they were made with. - `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_HEARTBEAT`: Each runner at its next heartbeat, and the workspaces running on it. - `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_REQUEST`: What is asked from now on - a project made, a shell opened, a workspace deleted; what was done before keeps the terms it was done under. - `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_PASS`: The next pass of the job that applies it: the autoscaler, the prebuilds' retirement, the collector's read of its policy, the daily look for a release.

One of: `SETTING_REACH_UNSPECIFIED`, `SETTING_REACH_RUNNING_WORKSPACES`, `SETTING_REACH_NEW_WORKSPACES`, `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_HEARTBEAT`, `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_REQUEST`, `SETTING_REACH_NEXT_PASS`.

## SettingType

SettingType is how a setting's value is written as text, which is how GetSettings answers it and SetSettings takes it. - `SETTING_TYPE_INT`: A whole number in decimal, within the definition's min and max. - `SETTING_TYPE_BOOL`: "true" or "false". - `SETTING_TYPE_STRING`: Text; a definition with choices takes only those. - `SETTING_TYPE_LIST`: A JSON array of strings. - `SETTING_TYPE_JSON`: A JSON document, as the code that reads it defines it. - `SETTING_TYPE_DURATION`: A Go duration ("60s"); min and max are seconds.

One of: `SETTING_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `SETTING_TYPE_INT`, `SETTING_TYPE_BOOL`, `SETTING_TYPE_STRING`, `SETTING_TYPE_LIST`, `SETTING_TYPE_JSON`, `SETTING_TYPE_DURATION`.

## SettingWriter

SettingWriter is who writes a setting, and so where an administrator changes it. - `SETTING_WRITER_ADMIN`: SetSettings, and the installation's file seeds it. - `SETTING_WRITER_FILE`: The installation's file alone: what whoever made the installation knows, and a change of which the dashboard cannot make whole - the proxy holds the base domain too. - `SETTING_WRITER_STORE`: A page of its own, which checks it against the real thing before it is written: the object store, the mail server. - `SETTING_WRITER_CONTROL_PLANE`: The control plane, for itself.

One of: `SETTING_WRITER_UNSPECIFIED`, `SETTING_WRITER_ADMIN`, `SETTING_WRITER_FILE`, `SETTING_WRITER_STORE`, `SETTING_WRITER_CONTROL_PLANE`.

## Snapshot

A snapshot is a rotation of a workspace's volume, published as a commit. It has no name outside its id.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |

| `state` | [SnapshotState](/reference/api/types/#snapshotstate) |  |
| `withMemory` | boolean | with_memory: the snapshot also kept the running machine's memory, so restoring it resumes the processes where they were instead of booting the disk. The memory is on the host the workspace ran on. |
| `parentSnapshotId` | string | The snapshot the disk this one was taken of had been cloned from. A restore gives the workspace a new disk cloned from the snapshot restored, so the snapshots with one parent are one disk's, and one whose parent is not ListSnapshotsResponse.base_snapshot_id was taken on a disk a restore left detached. Empty for a disk that was not cloned. |

One of: `SNAPSHOT_ACCESS_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `SNAPSHOT_ACCESS_TYPE_OWNER`, `SNAPSHOT_ACCESS_TYPE_SHARED`, `SNAPSHOT_ACCESS_TYPE_PUBLIC`.

## SnapshotState

How far along a snapshot is. A snapshot is taken by the host serving the volume, so it exists before it is usable: CREATING is the window between asking for one and the host reporting the commit it published. - `SNAPSHOT_STATE_CREATING`: Requested; the host has not published a commit yet - `SNAPSHOT_STATE_PUBLISHED`: Usable: a workspace can be created from it

One of: `SNAPSHOT_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `SNAPSHOT_STATE_CREATING`, `SNAPSHOT_STATE_PUBLISHED`, `SNAPSHOT_STATE_FAILED`, `SNAPSHOT_STATE_DELETING`.

## StatusDisagreementKind

- `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_SUPERVISOR_STALE`: The control plane says the workspace runs and the supervisor has gone quiet for longer than several heartbeat intervals. - `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_SUPERVISOR_ABSENT`: The control plane says the workspace runs and no supervisor ever reported. - `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_HOST_UNREACHABLE`: The host holding this workspace is not ACTIVE, or has stopped heartbeating. - `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_VOLUME_REFUSING`: The volume under the workspace is refusing to serve. - `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_UNHEALTHY`: The supervisor reports a failing health check.

One of: `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`, `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_SUPERVISOR_STALE`, `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_SUPERVISOR_ABSENT`, `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_HOST_UNREACHABLE`, `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_VOLUME_REFUSING`, `STATUS_DISAGREEMENT_KIND_UNHEALTHY`.

## StoredVolumeKind

- `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_WORKSPACE`: A workspace's disk, now or before. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_IMAGE`: An image a workspace's disk is cloned from. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_EXTENSION`: A release of an extension: the supervisor, the VS Code servers. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_UNCLAIMED`: A volume the database has and nothing names: a clone being made, or a delete not finished. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_ORPHAN`: Objects under a volume the database does not have. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_PREBUILD`: A prebuild: the disk of the workspace that built it, which the workspaces opened from it are cloned from. - `STORED_VOLUME_KIND_AGENT_HOME`: A person's agent's home, which outlives the workspaces that mount it.

## Workspace

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `teamId` | string | Every workspace has one: its owner's personal team unless another was named |
| `hostId` | string |  |
| `image` | string | Container image used for this workspace |
| `resources` | [Resources](/reference/api/types/#resources) |  |
| `state` | [WorkspaceState](/reference/api/types/#workspacestate) |  |
| `url` | string | Output only: https://{name}.{base domain}; empty until setup records a domain |
| `env` | map of string to string |  |
| `createdAt` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `updatedAt` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `snapshotCount` | integer (int32) | Number of snapshots in history |
| `failureReason` | string | Reason for failure (only set when state=FAILED) |
| `networkTags` | list of string | The network policies this workspace runs under, by name. Read back because what a workspace may reach is worth seeing without asking the host that enforces it. |
| `hostConnected` | boolean | host_connected says the host this workspace is on is talking to the control plane now. A workspace's state is its host's last word, and a host that stops talking stops correcting it: RUNNING is not transitional, so nothing fails it and nothing moves it, and a workspace whose machine died with its host reads as healthy for ever. The honest answer is not a different state - a host that cannot be reached may be running the machine perfectly well behind a broken network - but to say that the state is old and why. False for a workspace with no host at all (a stopped one), so read it beside the state. |
| `waitingReason` | string | waiting_reason is why a WAITING workspace has no host yet, as of the last attempt to place it: which runner was full of what, or that none is connected. Empty in every other state. |
| `failure` | [WorkspaceFailure](/reference/api/types/#workspacefailure) | failure is which part failed when state=FAILED, UNSPECIFIED in every other state: what a client says a person can do is decided by it, and failure_reason is the detail. |
| `networkWatch` | boolean | network_watch says its host records where it connects into its logs (SetWorkspaceNetworkWatch). |
| `floorCpuCores` | integer (int32) | What its preset started it at. resources.cpu_cores and memory_mb are what it holds now, and above these they are a grant (GrantWorkspaceResources). |
| `floorMemoryMb` | integer (int32) |  |
| `grantExpiresAt` | `Timestamp` | When its grant is given back on its own; unset for one kept until it is given back, and for a workspace holding none. |
| `quarantineHeld` | boolean | quarantine_held says a quarantine holds it: in force (state QUARANTINED), or asked for and its stop still on the way or ended FAILED. Until an administrator releases it, its own person cannot start, move or delete it, whatever the state says. |
| `progress` | [WorkspaceProgress](/reference/api/types/#workspaceprogress) | progress is where a transition is while one is under way - CREATING, STARTING, STOPPING, WAITING - and unset at rest: which attempt, why the one before failed, what the host is doing now, since when and until when before the control plane gives up on it. |
| `allowedActions` | list of [WorkspaceAction](/reference/api/types/#workspaceaction) | allowed_actions are what the server takes from this workspace as it is: its state, a quarantine's hold, and the failure it ended in. A client offers these and no others. |
| `failureSummary` | string | failure_summary says in a sentence what failed when state=FAILED, decided by failure: what a client shows above failure_reason, so the dashboard and the CLI say the same thing. What to do next is each client's, from allowed_actions. |
| `readyAt` | `Timestamp` | ready_at is when the workspace's supervisor answered for its current run: the workspace is usable, not only its machine handed off. Unset before, and while it is not running. |
| `traceId` | string | trace_id is the trace of the request that asked for its current generation, which runs through the host's operation and the state it reported. Empty when that request was not sampled. |
| `durability` | [WorkspaceDurability](/reference/api/types/#workspacedurability) | durability is how much of its disk is in the object store, in every state - running, stopped or suspended. Answered by GetWorkspace only, and only for a workspace with a volume: a listing does not ask every volume. |
| `role` | string | role is the caller's in it: "owner", or "guest" - who may connect, see it and open its ports, and nothing that changes it. |
| `checkoutPath` | string | checkout_path is where the workspace's project is checked out (projects.CheckoutPath), empty for a workspace that opened none: where its agent works unless told otherwise. GetWorkspace alone says it. |
| `memoryMachineGone` | boolean | memory_machine_gone says it is suspended with memory taken on a machine no host of the installation registers now (WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE_CHANGED): a start cannot resume it, and WORKSPACE_ACTION_START_FROM_DISK, which drops the memory, is what is offered instead. |
| `suspendsAt` | `Timestamp` | The question before a suspension: when the installation suspends it unless somebody keeps it (KeepWorkspace), asked ten minutes ahead, and which of the two suspensions is due (WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_IDLE_SUSPENDED or WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RUNNING_CAP_SUSPENDED). Unset while none is due within the warning: somebody used it since, or it is kept. |
| `suspendsFor` | [WorkspaceEventType](/reference/api/types/#workspaceeventtype) |  |
| `keptUntil` | `Timestamp` | An answer: kept awake until then, and neither suspension fires before it. |
| `leases` | list of [WorkspaceLease](/reference/api/types/#workspacelease) | The leases its processes hold, as its supervisor last reported them: while one is held and within the installation's workspace_lease_max_minutes of its start, nobody is asked, nothing idle is suspended, and the running cap waits for the lease's end. |
| `projectId` | string | The project it opened and the ref it was opened at; empty for a workspace that opened none. |
| `ref` | string |  |
| `wakeOnAccess` | boolean | Suspended, it is resumed by a signed-in visitor of one of its published ports (OpenWorkspaceProxySession). Never by an anonymous one: that would undo the idle suspension for whoever has a public port's URL. |
| `suspendedSnapshotId` | string | The snapshot it was suspended into: its next start resumes it rather than booting its disk. Empty when a start boots the disk - never suspended, resumed since, or the snapshot deleted. |
| `fromPrebuildId` | string | The prebuild its disk is a clone of; empty for one that opened with none. |
| `agentMinMemoryMb` | integer (int32) | What it has to hold for its agent to start there, in MB (the supervisor refuses below it). |
| `projectError` | string | project_error is what its guest last said went wrong with its project - the clone, its .spin.yaml or its create tasks - as the guest said it; empty when all of it went, or nothing has reported. The next boot tries again. A running workspace with one is DEGRADED. |
| `ownerId` | string | Whose it is: on a team's workspace, which member's. owner_id is in every answer; the name and email are answered by GetWorkspace and ListWorkspaces, whose callers - its owner and the guests its owner let in - are who may see it at all. |
| `ownerName` | string |  |
| `ownerEmail` | string |  |
| `hostClass` | string | host_class is the host class it runs on (HostClass.name), from its preset: placed only on a host of it, "default" where its preset named none. |
| `attempts` | list of [WorkspaceAttempt](/reference/api/types/#workspaceattempt) | attempts are the attempts its host failed at its current generation, oldest first: each one the host retried, and the last when the host ended the generation FAILED. Kept once it settles - FAILED says which attempt it was and what the ones before it hit - and gone with the next start, which is a new generation. An attempt whose report never reached the control plane is not here: the host reports why the attempt before failed, and a lost report is replaced by the next. |
| `projectReportedAt` | `Timestamp` | project_reported_at is when its guest said how its project went in this run, unset until it has: an empty project_error before then is a clone still going, not one that went. project_head is the commit it checked out, as the guest said it; empty when it did not say one. |
| `projectHead` | string |  |
| `hostName` | string | host_name is the name host_id's machine registered, for a person to tell hosts apart; empty with no host, or one that registered none. Answered by GetWorkspace and ListWorkspaces, so a list row says where each runs without a status read per row; never placed or trusted by. |
| `withoutPrebuild` | string | without_prebuild is why a workspace opening a project at a ref it prebuilds started from none of its prebuilds, and cloned the repository at its first boot: none ready, the ready one of another image, its disk not cloneable yet. Empty with from_prebuild_id set, or for a project that prebuilds nothing. |

## WorkspaceAction

WorkspaceAction is an act a person can ask of a workspace. - `WORKSPACE_ACTION_FORCE_STOP`: Stop without waiting for the guest: also what ends a stop that does not finish. - `WORKSPACE_ACTION_SUSPEND`: Put down with its memory, to be resumed where it was. - `WORKSPACE_ACTION_START_FROM_DISK`: Boot a suspended workspace from its disk, dropping its memory (StartWorkspaceRequest.from_disk): offered when that memory's machine is run by no host (Workspace.memory_machine_gone).

One of: `WORKSPACE_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_START`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_STOP`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_FORCE_STOP`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_DELETE`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_FORCE_DELETE`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_SUSPEND`, `WORKSPACE_ACTION_START_FROM_DISK`.

## WorkspaceDurability

WorkspaceDurability is what of a workspace's disk is published, so it survives its host. While a host serves the disk - running, or stopped with its disk kept there - it is that host's last report; once none does - suspended, or its disk handed back to the store - it is the newest published snapshot of the disk (snapshot_id), which is what a start boots from.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `lastPublishedAt` | `Timestamp` | last_published_at is when its last commit reached the object store, as its host last said; from a snapshot, when that snapshot was taken. |
| `unpublishedSeconds` | string (int64) | What is written and not yet published, as of the host's report plus the time since. |
| `unpublishedBytes` | string (int64) |  |
| `stalled` | boolean | stalled says publishing has not kept up with the bound it runs to (the volume's RPO). |
| `reportedAt` | `Timestamp` | reported_at is the host's report these are as of; unset when they are a snapshot's. |
| `snapshotId` | string | snapshot_id is the published snapshot the last copy is, when no host serves the disk, and published_bytes how much of the disk it holds. Empty and zero while they are a host's report. |
| `publishedBytes` | string (int64) |  |

## WorkspaceEventType

- `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_CREATED`: Workspace was created - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STARTED`: Workspace was started - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STOPPED`: Workspace was stopped; its disk is kept, and no snapshot is taken - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_SNAPSHOT_CREATED`: Manual snapshot - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_DELETED`: Workspace was deleted - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_FAILED`: Workspace start failed - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RESTORED`: Its disk was put back to a snapshot - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RESUMED`: It went on from a snapshot's memory - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_BOOTED`: Suspended, its memory could not be resumed, and its disk was booted - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_QUARANTINED`: An administrator held it: stopped, and startable by nobody until released - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNQUARANTINED`: The hold was released: back to stopped, where it was held from - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_PLACED`: A workspace that waited for a host was given one, and its disk there - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_TRASHED`: Deleted into the trash: its disk kept, its owner able to undelete it - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNDELETED`: Taken back out of the trash - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_MOVED`: Suspended on its host and resumed on another, which had room for what it was granted - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_DISPLACED`: Its host was drained or went away: suspended there, it is resumed on another on its own - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STOP_BACKUP_FAILED`: A stop on a host that can be taken away could not publish its disk first, so it runs on - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_IDLE_SUSPENDED`: Nobody used it for as long as the installation allows: suspended with its processes, a start resumes them - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RUNNING_CAP_SUSPENDED`: It ran at a stretch for as long as the installation allows: suspended with its processes, a start resumes them - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_SUSPENSION_DUE`: A suspension is minutes away and the question was asked: its terminals, its page, the CLI; a keep answers it - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_KEPT`: Somebody kept it awake until a time: no suspension before it - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNRESPONSIVE`: Its supervisor said nothing for longer than the control plane waits: stopped by force, and a start brings it back - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_REHOMED`: Its host stopped answering and it was moved to another on its own, giving up what that host had not published - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_HELD`: Its host stopped answering and moving it would give up more than the installation does on its own: it waits for its owner - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RECOVERED_BY_ADMIN`: An administrator moved it off a host that is gone, giving up for its owner what that host had not published; its details say who and why - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_OUT_OF_MEMORY`: It ran out of memory: its guest's kernel killed a process (cause "guest", with the kills and their victims), its host found it short at its ceiling for a while (cause "ceiling"), or its host killed the machine (cause "host"). Its details say what it held, its grant and its ceiling. Said, never acted on: nothing resizes a workspace on its own. - `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_OVERSIZED`: It held far more than it used for a week: the most memory its processes used stayed under half its own, and a smaller preset would fit what it used. Its details say what it used, what it holds, and that preset. Said, never acted on: nothing resizes a workspace on its own.

One of: `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_CREATED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STARTED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STOPPED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_SNAPSHOT_CREATED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_DELETED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_FAILED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RESTORED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RESUMED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_BOOTED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_QUARANTINED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNQUARANTINED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_PLACED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_TRASHED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNDELETED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_MOVED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_DISPLACED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_STOP_BACKUP_FAILED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_IDLE_SUSPENDED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RUNNING_CAP_SUSPENDED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_SUSPENSION_DUE`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_KEPT`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_UNRESPONSIVE`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_REHOMED`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_HELD`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RECOVERED_BY_ADMIN`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_OVERSIZED`.

## WorkspaceFailure

WorkspaceFailure is why a FAILED workspace failed: which part of its run, closed so what a person can do about it - and a failure rate split by the repair it needs - is decided by the kind rather than by the text of an error. The reason beside it is the detail. One enum for the client and the host's report (spin.agent.v1.ObservedWorkspace): the kind a person is shown is the one the host named, with no second list to keep in step. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not classified. A failure that lands here is a site missing its classification. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_VOLUME`: Its disk could not be served or made: the host is not serving its volume (its refusal says why), or what the disk was to be made from is gone. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXTENSION`: An extension could not be attached, or the releases it starts with could not be named. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NETWORK`: The machine's network namespace or its tags could not be set up. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RESOURCES`: The machine could not be given the cores or memory it was asked for. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE`: QEMU could not be prepared or did not boot. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_GUEST`: The guest booted and did not take its identity or its own filesystem. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RELEASE_GONE`: A resume needs an extension release that is no longer in the object store: the memory cannot be resumed anywhere, and the control plane boots the disk with the newest releases. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXITED`: The machine ended without being asked to, and not by a panic of its guest's kernel: its guest reset it, or its QEMU was killed, exited with an error or crashed. The detail says which. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_STOP`: The machine could not be stopped or removed. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_TIMED_OUT`: Its host did not bring a start or a stop to an end before the deadline: unreachable, or its attempts outlasted it. The control plane's verdict (the stuck sweep), never a host's. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NO_HOST`: No host could take it: none came with room while it waited, or its disk is only on a host that is not connected. The control plane's verdict, never a host's. - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE_CHANGED`: Its memory was taken on a machine no host of the installation runs now: the machine's contract moved (a release that changed it), or the processor did. The memory resumes nowhere; the workspace stays suspended, and booting it from its disk, which drops the memory, is its owner's to choose (StartWorkspaceRequest.from_disk). - `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_GUEST_PANIC`: The guest's kernel panicked, which ended its machine. The cause is inside the guest: the detail quotes the console's panic line, and the console has what led to it.

One of: `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_VOLUME`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXTENSION`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NETWORK`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RESOURCES`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_GUEST`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_RELEASE_GONE`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_EXITED`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_STOP`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_TIMED_OUT`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_NO_HOST`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_MACHINE_CHANGED`, `WORKSPACE_FAILURE_GUEST_PANIC`.

## WorkspaceNetworkStatus

WorkspaceNetworkStatus is one policy a workspace runs under, and whether it holds there: the installation declares it, and the workspace's host reports having installed it. A tag no policy is declared for, or one its host has not installed, is what a start is refused over.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `policy` | string |  |
| `declared` | boolean | declared says a policy of this name exists: the installation's, or a team's. |
| `installed` | boolean | installed says the workspace's host last reported enforcing a policy of this name. False for a workspace on no host. |

## WorkspacePhase

WorkspacePhase is what a host is doing to bring a workspace up. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_DISK`: Waiting for its disk to be served on the host. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_EXTENSIONS`: Holding the extension releases it runs with. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_NETWORK`: Setting up its network. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_MACHINE`: Booting its machine, or resuming it from a checkpoint. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_FIRST_BOOT`: Its first boot of a disk another person's workspace was cloned from. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_GUEST`: The machine is up and its workspace inside is starting. - `WORKSPACE_PHASE_BACKUP`: Stopping on a host that can be taken away: its disk is being published before the machine stops, the control plane's doing rather than the host's, and retried if it restarts.

One of: `WORKSPACE_PHASE_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_DISK`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_EXTENSIONS`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_NETWORK`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_MACHINE`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_FIRST_BOOT`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_GUEST`, `WORKSPACE_PHASE_BACKUP`.

## WorkspaceProgress

WorkspaceProgress is a transition under way.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `attempt` | integer (int32) | attempt is the host's attempt at the current generation, from 1, and attempts how many it makes before the workspace fails. Zero before the host has made one. |
| `attempts` | integer (int32) |  |
| `lastFailure` | [WorkspaceFailure](/reference/api/types/#workspacefailure) | Why the attempt before this one failed, while this one is in progress: what a retry hides. |
| `lastReason` | string |  |
| `phase` | [WorkspacePhase](/reference/api/types/#workspacephase) | phase is what the host is doing now; UNSPECIFIED when it has not said. |
| `since` | `Timestamp` | since is when the transition began, and deadline when the control plane gives up on it - a wait for a host, or a start or a stop the host does not finish - and fails the workspace. |
| `deadline` | `Timestamp` |  |
| `typical` | `Duration` | typical is how long a start usually takes on the workspace's host class: the median, from the request to RUNNING (the same measure as since), of the newest starts that came up there. Unset for a transition that is not a start, and where too few have come up to say. Per step it is not: what a host says of its phases is kept only while one is under way. |

## WorkspaceProxyStatus

Proxy status for workspace access - `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_ACCESSIBLE`: Port exposed, workspace running - `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_NOT_RUNNING`: Return 503 - `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`: Return 404 - `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_PORT_NOT_EXPOSED`: Return 403 - `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_WAKING`: Not running, and woken for this caller (Workspace.wake_on_access): the proxy opens a session, which resumes it and waits a while, and shows a page that asks again while it is not up.

One of: `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_ACCESSIBLE`, `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_NOT_RUNNING`, `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_PORT_NOT_EXPOSED`, `WORKSPACE_PROXY_STATUS_WAKING`.

## WorkspaceRuntime

WorkspaceRuntime is a running workspace's machine as its host measures it from outside the guest. Answers "is my workspace out of memory" and "did it get the cores it borrowed" for the one person asking, which no metric may: those are labelled by host, never by workspace.

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `cpuCores` | integer (int32) |  |
| `memoryBytes` | string (int64) |  |
| `memoryUsedBytes` | string (int64) |  |
| `cpuSeconds` | number (double) |  |
| `machineStartedAt` | `Timestamp` |  |

## WorkspaceState

WorkspaceState is where a workspace is in its life. Each value's comment is what the API's document says of it (buf.gen.openapi.yaml's with-enum-value-descriptions), and the website's table of states is generated from it: it is written for a person reading that table, in the site's words (a runner, the CLI's commands). Why a value is what it is goes in a comment apart, above the value's own, which the document does not carry. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never a workspace's state: a client that reads it read a field nothing set. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_CREATING`: The workspace exists and has not run yet. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_STARTING`: A runner is preparing its disk and starting its machine. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_RUNNING`: Its machine is up. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPING`: Its machine is shutting down, and then what its disk wrote since its last commit is uploaded to the bucket. A stop stays here until the upload is done, and says why it is not; `spin workspace stop --force` does not wait for it. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPED`: Not running. Its disk is kept, and the next start boots from it. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_FAILED`: A start or a stop failed: `spin workspace status` says which part, and why. It stays so until it is started again. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_DELETED`: In the trash, with its disk, for the days the installation keeps it there (`workspace_trash_days`): `spin workspace undelete` brings it back, stopped. An installation that keeps no trash erases it at once. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_WAITING`: Wanted running, and no runner has room for it yet. On AWS, where runners scale to none, one is being started, and the workspace starts on it once it is up. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_QUARANTINED`: Held by an administrator with `spin workspace quarantine`: it cannot start until `spin workspace unquarantine` releases it, and its disk is kept as it was. - `WORKSPACE_STATE_DEGRADED`: Its machine is up, and what was asked of it inside did not finish: its project's checkout, .spin.yaml or create tasks. Everything a running workspace allows is allowed; `spin workspace get` says what failed, and the next boot tries again.

One of: `WORKSPACE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_CREATING`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_STARTING`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_RUNNING`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPING`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_STOPPED`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_FAILED`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_DELETED`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_WAITING`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_QUARANTINED`, `WORKSPACE_STATE_DEGRADED`.

## WritebackPreset

| `backgroundBytes` | string (int64) |  |
| `measured` | string | measured is what it did, in words. |
